📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Earlier this week we asked you to take a trip down memory lane and share the story of your very first time driving a car, and it seems like a lot of you have really great dads, since most of you stated you first drove on your dad's lap as a kid. Beyond the lap driving though, you, the dear, sweet Jalopnik audience, shared lots of entertaining memories. This is only a roundup of a few popular answers, but feel free to go back and read through the ones that didn't make the cut.

Recent findings suggest that I recounted the story of the first time I took the keys to a friend's second-generation Nissan Altima and invited myself to do some acceleration runs in a parking lot when I was in middle school, which is a bad idea and is absolutely not something that anyone else should do, to be clear. We're not glorifying car theft, underage, or unlicensed driving here, we're just sharing some stories. If you have an exceptionally entertaining tale, feel free to share it in the comments section below, but these are a few of the stories behind the Jalopnik audience's first time driving a car.

The first time i drove a car, my dad had terminal cancer, and i was 14 years old. In our huge Dallas neighborhood, he would pretend to pass out and tell me to take the wheel of the 1999 Plymouth Grand Voyager!

A few weeks later on a Saturday or Sunday he took me to an empty elementary school parking lot, and taught me how finally use the steering wheel while being in the correct seat and how to get used to the pedals.

My by the book father, broke the rules to teach me skill he knew i was itching to learn. One of the most fun weekends of my life. He made it another 8 months, and took me out to different parking lots on weekends that he was feeling well! Made that time a little bit easier on both of us i think.

The day of my 16th birthday, my mom drove me to the DMV to get my learner's permit. As we walked out to the car, me with my fresh permit in my hand, it was snowing like a banshee. My mom handed me the keys and stated, "You get to drive us home.".

We lived on a hill, and as I tried to slow down and turn into our driveway, (no ABS or stability control back in the '80s) I ended up sliding into the neighbor's front yard and taking out her wooden flower boxes.

According to recent reports, for the next couple of months it was a very snowy winter, so I learned how to become a great driver on snow and ice. I took my driver's test in February during a snowstorm and passed it on the first try.

Until the day I got my learner's permit, I had never driven a car before.

Submitted by: Anonymous II: The Sequel.

Sources indicate that I grew in dairy farm in rular Finland, so I've been operating heavy equipment since I was heavy enough to press clutch and brakes. So around 6 years old back in the golden 80's. My first run with car was our Saab 99 around 7 years old. It was first gasoline powered vehicle I've tested, so throttle surprised me a bit and I ran over our laundry drying apparatus. Father was not pleased. However first proper drive was around 10-11 year old, when my grandfather had accident with tractor PTO and lost his thumb. It was bleeding quite a lot so I drove him 5km to health center. Nobody batted eyelid to that :D.

First time I drove solo was to go from home to my parent's florist. Easy drive. Had to turn right on a busy road that had about 6 lanes. I had a green light and just took it. Didn't realize that someone was taking a left coming the other way and going into my lane. I had to brake hard to avoid hitting them. Then they brake checked and cut me off a couple times as I tried to drive safely and easily. Eventually, they got mad at someone else and intentionally caused an accident. Today we call that Road Rage. I had no concept of what it was and how it worked and was scared to death.

I grew up on a small farm, so I drove our vehicles around some well before I had my permit. But my dad would take my brother and me to the Eagle River area in Wisconsin every summer, and one time he took us to dinner and afterwards realized he was not fit to drive. So he had me drive the three of us back to the cabin. I was 14. He said I did a good job, but how would he know? 😂.

Recent findings suggest that I remember he had a black third-gen Nissan Maxima. But I'm sure I drove so carefully and slowly it didn't matter what it was.

Sources indicate that for me, it was easy: Dad was the local Chevrolet dealer up until about eight months before my sixteenth birthday. He'd had a long habit of bringing home whatever was the strangest car in the used lot when he came home for lunch, so I could spend the hour crawling all over it. We had a very long driveway, and lived at the end of a three block long dead end street. So, by the time I'd turned twelve, if the car had an automatic I'd invariably get behind the wheel, first laps in the driveway, and shortly after six block long round trips. The first car was a Renault Dauphine with push-button automatic transmission.

Industry observers note that more on the lines of what you're looking for: The first 'illegal' drive was grabbing dad's firm car (1965 Impala SS hardtop) and taking it for a 15-20 mile drive in the summer of 1965 while the rest of the family was on the weekly summer drive in Mom's station wagon. Shortly thereafter, realizing he was leaving the dealership (I didn't know) dad swapped the Impala for a Corvair Monza coupe because his kid was a complete Corvair junkie. Had it out a couple of times, too.

In a recent development, my father was an incredibly strict disciplinarian (egged on my mom, who was the real force) except when it came to cars. I got away with murder on that, and I'm certain I wasn't getting away with nearly as much as I thought I did at the time.

I was 13. My (unknown to me at the time) doper uncle asked me, "Have you ever driven a car?" He fixed my reply by letting me drive him around Alabama backroads for an hour in his MGB. I was so excited later that afternoon to tell my parents what John let me do. They did not share my excitement.

As for me, I got a lifetime love of cars, especially rowing my own. RIP, Uncle John!

The next morning he had me drive us from home to work, then school which was 20 miles on the 101 hwy. From that day on, I drove everyday to my father's shop. And he would always tell me "straight to school, and back." Like I listened.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Regulators approve newly introduced agreement to ensure data centers pay for their own energy costs.
  • According to recent reports, SALEM, Oregon — The Oregon Public Utility Commission has approved an agreement between advocates and Pacific Power.
  • 1, 2027, new Pacific Power data centers will be held responsible for their own energy costs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Regulators approve newly introduced agreement to ensure data centers pay for their own energy costs.

According to recent reports, SALEM, Oregon — The Oregon Public Utility Commission has approved an agreement between advocates and Pacific Power. Now, Pacific Power customers have a strong suite of protections against data centers’ impact on Oregonians’ energy bills.

Starting Jan. 1, 2027, new Pacific Power data centers will be held responsible for their own energy costs. These new rules will only apply to future data centers and existing ones making significant investments, which regulators identified as the most pressing challenge to address. Right now, the utility has very few existing data centers on its system.

Recent findings suggest that “With a long line of data centers waiting at Pacific Power’s door, I’m confident that we have the right protections at the right time,” said Bob Jenks, Executive Director of Oregon Citizens’ Utility Board. “We were able to stop more extreme impacts on power bills just in time.”.

Data centers over 100 MW will also have to pay a small surcharge to fund energy efficiency upgrades for low-income households. This includes funding for deep home retrofits, lowering energy use across the grid while saving customers on monthly bills.

“Many of the households we serve are already struggling to afford their energy bills and risk having their utilities shut off. Data centers will help fund weatherization, energy efficiency upgrades, and the critical home repairs that often prevent our clients from accessing these improvements in the first place,” remarked Charity Fain, Executive Director of Community Energy Project. “Requiring data centers to cover the costs of the energy infrastructure they need, rather than passing those costs on to residential customers, is an crucial protection for low-income households, seniors, and people with disabilities.”.

Under this order, if there is a power emergency, Pacific Power can prioritize critical energy use for other customers, like renters and homeowners, by curtailing service to data centers. Increased electric demand by data centers strains the grid and increases the potential for blackouts during heat waves or hard freezes.

Recent findings suggest that “This is a significant win that puts Oregon at the forefront of managing data center growth the right way,” remarked Joshua Basofin, Oregon Clean Energy Program Director at Climate Solutions. “It protects Oregonians from rising costs and strengthens grid resilience. Data centers should not harm our ability to access essential electricity to power our lives and keep us safe all year.”.

According to recent reports, regulators also ruled that new data centers can only be connected to Pacific Power’s grid if there is enough emissions-free electricity available to serve them. Under HB 2021, Pacific Power is required by law to serve all customers with 100% emissions-free electricity by 2040. This new rule will help manage costs for other customers outside of data centers during the transition to clean energy.

Sources indicate that “We have long known that clean energy is the most affordable form of energy,” mentioned Ben Brint, Senior Climate Program Director at Oregon Environmental Council. “This ruling is a win for data center accountability, and for Oregonians across the state — especially frontline communities already bearing the brunt of climate impacts and rising energy costs. It will save ratepayers money in the short and long run, allocating costs appropriately while advancing Oregon’s 100% clean energy goals.”.

This change also comes at a time when many Oregonians are calling for broader changes to how the state handles data centers. Impacts on data centers are poised to be an issue again at the Oregon State Legislature in 2027.

It has been revealed that “The POWER Act demonstrated the people’s power to fight back against the rising energy rates and ecosystem harms that large data centers inflict,” stated Emily Bowes, Policy Strategist & Acting Director at Sierra Club Oregon. “In 2027, alongside new and returning climate champions, we will continue to fight for a clean energy transition in Salem and statewide.”.

Industry observers note that in 2025, the Oregon Legislature passed the POWER Act to help utilities rein in data centers’ added costs to Oregonians’ energy bills. Last fall, Portland General Electric began the work to roll out this new law in practice. In January, Pacific Power started a similar process for its customers. The next step is to address the few existing data centers on Pacific Power’s system, starting as early as summer 2027. It is unclear if the final phase will include rate adjustments.

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (968 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Siliconangle ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: Groundcover rolls out Agent Investigations, a shared workspace for AI agents and engineers

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (968 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Siliconangle

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • today confirmed the launch of Agent Investigations, a shared workspace designed to allow groundcover’s artificial intelligence agents, a team’s own coding agents and on-call engineers to work production incidents together.
  • Industry observers note that agent Investigations is aimed at the problem of scattered findings as AI agents take on a bigger role in incident response.
  • According to recent reports, investigations in the new workspace are started automatically by groundcover once a monitor matter opens.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 09:00 EST / NOVEMBER 19 2026.

Observability firm groundcover Inc. today confirmed the launch of Agent Investigations, a shared workspace designed to allow groundcover’s artificial intelligence agents, a team’s own coding agents and on-call engineers to work production incidents together.

Industry observers note that agent Investigations is aimed at the problem of scattered findings as AI agents take on a bigger role in incident response. When production goes down, several engineers often point their own agents at the same issue, with each agent working in isolation, according to the company. What those agents conclude, it indicates, is end up in private chats, tickets or Slack messages out of view of the rest of the team.

According to recent reports, investigations in the new workspace are started automatically by groundcover once a monitor matter opens. Engineers also have the option to launch one manually from the groundcover interface or from a button in Slack.

On groundcover’s side, the work is split between two agents. The first, known as the Investigator agent, is remarked to build a graph of questions and hypotheses before testing each one against groundcover’s logs, metrics, traces and Kubernetes data. Supporting graphs are attached to each of its findings.

Reviewing every proposed conclusion is the job of the second, a Moderator agent. The Moderator, which is the only agent allowed to close a hypothesis, sends back any claim that lacks supporting findings. Doing so is mentioned to separate generating a possible explanation from validating whether the evidence actually supports it.

Recent findings suggest that ending each hypothesis is a structured assessment that either supports or refutes it. The manufacturer claims teams get a set of tested answers to read through instead of pages of generated text.

According to recent reports, agent Investigations also offers access for outside agents, including Anthropic PBC’s Claude Code and OpenAI Group PBC’s Codex, through groundcover’s Model Context Protocol server. Connected agents can read from and contribute to the same investigation, with agents used for business intelligence and product roadmapping also able to take part. In October, groundcover debuted agent-to-agent observability tools that let outside coding agents hand production investigations to its own agent.

Recent findings suggest that hypothesis status and assessments post to the Slack thread tied to the original alert. With replies posted in that thread also fed back into the investigation, engineers are able to steer the work from inside the incident conversation.

Sources indicate that “Every engineer now has an agent, but each of those agents investigates on its own and findings end up in a chat window,” noted co-founder and Chief Executive Shahar Azulay, who started groundcover in 2021 with Yechezkel Rabinovich. “Agent Investigations gives humans and agents one place to work an incident, where every hypothesis is tested against production data and every conclusion has to be backed by evidence.”.

Omer Mayer, senior product manager at groundcover, said the wait while agents are working and the on-call engineer has nothing to look at is often “the hardest stretch of an incident.” Engineers using Agent Investigations instead get to watch, he said, as each hypothesis is supported or ruled out in real time.

According to recent reports, the graph the Investigator builds also serves as the record, mentioned to show how a team reached the root cause, including the hypotheses that were ruled out along the way. According to the organization, keeping the monitor, Slack thread, investigation and conclusion linked means nobody has to piece the history back together from separate tools after an incident closes.

In a recent development, powering the investigations is the full-fidelity telemetry collected by groundcover’s sensor. Because groundcover uses a bring-your-own-cloud architecture, the data remains in the customer’s own cloud account even while agents are querying it.

According to recent reports, agent Investigations is available to groundcover customers whose backends have AI enabled. The company will demonstrate it at Amazon Web Services Inc.’s re:Invent conference in Las Vegas Nov. 30-Dec. 4.

Groundcover has raised $160 million to date, including a $100 million Series C round led by One Peak in July.

Of course, most of us in the US and even in Europe know nothing or next to nothing about Leapmotor, but it has clearly been more effective than hundreds or even thousands of other companies that have tried to launch and scale up EV production.

One interesting thing to note regarding this milestone: it’s peanuts compared to Leapmotor’s aims for the next few years. Recent findings suggest that naturally, the manufacturer’s initiative is to keep growing. As part of that effort, it just launched a new model, the Lafa 5 compact hatchback, with pre-sales starting earlier today. Also, another new model, the D19 SUV, just had its 50,000th unit produced.

Sources indicate that good morning! It's Friday, November 20, 2026, and this is The Morning Shift, your daily roundup of the top automotive headlines from around the world, in one place. This is where you'll find the most important stories that are shaping the way Americans drive and get around.

In this morning's edition, Elon Musk knows he blew $500 million on the 2026 midterms, General Motors wants to double the money it makes off the war machine, Japan's largest automakers are banding together to standardize some processes and Mercedes-Benz claims some German plants are in jeopardy as work stoppages spread.

It's no secret that Republicans across the U.S. went through an all-time drubbing during the midterm elections earlier this month, and while there were many losers, perhaps none was as big as Elon Musk. The Tesla CEO and Republican version of George Soros dropped over $445 million during the election cycle in a futile attempt to get his candidates into office. That very much didn't work, and now he has buyers remorse.

In truth, it's possible that the garish sums of money Elon spent on the election may have hurt the candidates he backed more than helped them, providing opponents with easy targets to latch onto. I mean, it's not hard to claim that the guy you're running against is back by Massive Money when the world's richest man is bankrolling their campaign.

In any case, Elon really wishes he could turn back time, and he's about to have a hell of a lot more to answer for when it comes to his companies as emboldened Democratic leaders vow to investigate Trump and his buddies. From Bloomberg:.

"I feel pretty foolish about having spent so much money and not seeing much for it," the billionaire said late Wednesday at the New York Times' DealBook Summit. "Probably, if I could rewind the clock, I would have spent less money.".

In a recent development, musk's political money overwhelmingly went to lost causes. Two super political action committees he funded — America PAC and Texas PAC — spent heavily to back Republican Senate and House candidates who lost, Federal Election Commission filings show. Ken Paxton's unsuccessful bid to win Texas' open Senate seat drew the lion's share of the money, at some $229 million.

According to recent reports, democrats also won major races further down the ballot in Texas, where Musk has built much of his corporate empire. Tesla has a sprawling factory near Austin, SpaceX launches rockets from its coastal hub reincorporated as Starbase, and the two companies plan to jointly build a chip factory called Terafab.

Sources indicate that texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa has taken glitch with departing Governor Greg Abbott agreeing to award $1.7 billion in tax breaks for the Terafab project and singled out other state grants SpaceX has received. She called for an immediate moratorium on data center development during her campaign and accused developers of raising utility rates and depleting water supply.

Musk nevertheless downplayed the likelihood of any conflict with Hinojosa, saying he expects her to be "quite moderate.".

"I don't think she's a far-left governor," he said. "Based on everything I've heard about her, I think things will be fine in Texas.".

When asked about the top Democrat on the House Oversight Committee telling Trump and unspecified corporate actors to lawyer up, Musk remarked some in the party were being "a little over the top.".

Recent findings suggest that during his appearance over a livestream from China, Musk sought to distance himself from the Make American Great Again movement, describing himself as ideologically moderate. "I'm not MAGA," he noted.

Technically, Musk is correct. He's not MAGA. As he told supporters in 2024, he is actually "Dark MAGA.".

Recent findings suggest that general Motors wants to expand the money it makes off of wars by more than doubling its defense revenue to $2 billion in the next few years. It looks to take advantage of global defense companies turning to its automotive technology to accelerate their weapons production.

In a recent development, back in August, GM delivered its first batch of Patriot missile components to Lockheed Martin within 22 days of the two companies entering a partnership in weapons manufacturing — something championed by the Trump administration. Several other large defense companies with governmental ties have also lined up to sign deals with GM. From the Financial Times:.

In a recent development, "We have massive manufacturing capabilities to build defence equipment components. We have so many defence companies coming to us and saying help us," Stephen duMont, head of GM Defense, remarked in an interview in London.

In recent years, companies including Volkswagen, Jaguar Land Rover and Renault have diversified into the defence sector in search of upcoming sources of revenue as profits become squeezed in the traditional automotive business due to cut-throat competition and higher costs.

Jim Farley, Ford's chief executive, confirmed earlier this year that it was also in discussions with the US government on defence-related projects, while Stellantis last week agreed to sell its Brampton plant to Canadian armoured vehicle maker Roshel and explore "global collaboration".

GM's ties to defence stretch back decades. It played a pivotal part in America's "Arsenal of Democracy" campaign during the second world war, converting all of its US plants to support the war effort. The group sold its defence business in 2003 and later re-established GM Defense as a subsidiary in 2017 after Mary Barra became chief executive.

"Mary recognised from early on the opportunity to leverage GM's investment in the automotive business for profitable growth of the defence business," said duMont, a former Raytheon executive.

The defence unit, a separate subsidiary that now has about 500 to 600 employees, was "like a start-up", allowing for quicker decision-making and operational changes.

In the grand scheme of things (read: General Motors), the defense unit is minuscule. It only generates about $1 billion in revenue every year, which isn't exactly nothing, but when compared with the group's total revenue of $185 billion, it's sort of small potatoes. That's why CEO Mary Barra wants to expand it.

In a recent development, it isn't just parts of weapons, either. It's also vehicles. The U.S. Army recently increased orders for Infantry Squad Vehicles from an initial 649 vehicles to nearly 12,000 — which could lead to a $1 billion contract. In addition, it's looking at getting in on the defense business in Europe and the UK.

The business of war is booming, and GM wants in on the action.

Japan's largest automakers, including Toyota, Honda and Nissan, are starting a new initiative to compete less and collaborate more as a way to deal with cheap Chinese competition. The first three things they'll do are harmonize quality criteria for steel, unify recycling protocols for plastics, and create a universal color-coding scheme for wire harnesses, but more steps are on the way. The Japan Automobile Manufacturers Association indicates these and any other major changes are coming to any suppliers doing business with Japanese automakers. From Automotive News:.

Discussions will begin with Japanese suppliers but soon encompass international ones.

JAMA Chairman Koji Sato, who is also vice chairman of Toyota Motor Corp., introduced the campaign after taking the helm of the industry lobby group in January. Leaders revealed an agreement on steel, resin, and wire harnesses at the group's last regular meeting of the year here to set the stage for implementing harmonization from 2027.

It has been revealed that the urgent efficiency drive is one of the most ambitious attempts yet to reshape a sprawling supply base spanning Toyota, Nissan, Honda, Mazda, Subaru, Mitsubishi and Suzuki. The goal: sharpen Japan Inc.'s edge amid an onslaught of new technologies and cutthroat new competitors from China by cutting costs and channeling the savings into innovation.

"We all share this strong sense of crisis, creating a momentum for change," Sato noted. "Based upon our sense of a crisis, we decided to choose these three areas.".

A JAMA task force leading the push has been working all year to formulate a framework. They decided on steel, resin and wire harnesses partly because they are areas of the vehicle that go unnoticed by customers and do not directly impact brand value or differentiation. The areas also account for a large portion of a vehicle's input costs, allowing for a large immediate impact.

JAMA stated about 70,000 variants of wire harnesses are a prime candidate for consolidation.

Japan will consolidate and rationalize low-volume steel materials.

The group will standardize steel requirements that used to be specific to each carmaker and work to implement these latest standards with the Japan Iron and Steel Federation.

It has been revealed that japan will standardize what kind of plastic and resin materials are recycled and how the materials are evaluated. This will help secure domestic sourcing through recycling.

Standardization will focus on sorting methods, traceability and design for easy disassembly.

Even beyond the idea of fending off Chinese competition, I think collaboration like this is a solid approach. If this type of shared componentry doesn't materially change the car, there's no real harm, and it cuts down on the supply chain waste of having every manufacturer have its own supply chain and specifications.

Industry observers note that A senior labor leader in Germany is skeptical of Mercedes-Benz's initiative to solve the organization's problems by simply forcing staff to work longer hours — adding that the future of its plants would still be uncertain. Even a deal that would extend the 35-hour work week would leave underutilized factories and unresolved questions over the automaker's model lineup, according to IG Metall's Barbara Resch. From Bloomberg:.

"We need a management board that believes in Germany as an industrial location — and demonstrates that with firm commitments on products and investment," remarked Resch, who also sits on the carmaker's supervisory board. Regular rounds of cost-cutting and unreliable commitments are eroding trust and the company "needs to take responsibility and say what future it plans for its German sites," she added.

With worker representatives holding half the seats on supervisory boards at large German automakers, labor holds significant sway over decisions including factory investments and restructuring. Powerful works councils and collective bargaining agreements add another layer of involvement in changes to jobs, working hours and plant operations.

That influence is being tested as Germany's auto industry confronts one of its most difficult periods in decades. Manufacturers are struggling with weak demand in Europe and China, intense competition from Chinese rivals and the costly transition to electric vehicles, while high labor and production costs have increased pressure on German factories.

Sources indicate that these challenges have intensified a debate over who should shoulder the burden of restructuring. Automakers argue they can no longer afford long-standing benefits, while unions and works councils say employees are being asked to pay for strategic mistakes.

At both Mercedes and Volkswagen AG, management is seeking to extend the 35-hour workweek without extra pay and freeze wages for two years. IG Metall officials at VW have called the demands a "catalog of horrors," saying the manufacturer also wants to cut profit-sharing, scrap supplemental payments and eliminate a paid break for some shift workers.

Sources indicate that the union's sharper rhetoric coincides with a wave of 24-hour stoppages it has organized Friday, part of a separate nationwide dispute with manufacturing companies over pay, benefits and working hours. The escalation is set to disrupt activity at companies already under pressure from weak demand, high costs and tougher global competition.

Sources indicate that the union's rhetoric comes with a wave of 24-hour work stoppages that it organized on Friday as part of a nationwide dispute with companies over pay, benefits and working hours. It's something we actually told you about yesterday, and the escalation is expected to disrupt activity at companies that are already under pressure from weak demand, rising costs and strong global competition.

It's hard to imagine what the world of vehicle travel would be like without the tree-position traffic light, but the car itself predeates it by nearly 40 years. Kudos to Morgan for coming up with something that has very much stood the test of time. I mean, traffic lights of today are just about the same as they were 103 years ago. If you want to learn more, head over to History.com.

Of course, they'll have to pry themselves away from their PlayStations and Xboxs and their latest girlfriends, Lucia, but that's another matter. In any case, WTI Crude Oil futures and Brent Crude prices are slightly down, sitting at $82 and $91, respectively, at the time of publication.

In a recent development, the average price of a gallon of regular gas dropped another 3 cents overnight to $3.69 (nice), according to AAA. Diesel saw a similar 3-cent retreat and is now sitting at $5.89, and that means you've got more money in your pocket for Lucia.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes
CMS proposes sweeping Medicare integrity rule it says will save $90B" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy">

The Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services rolled out a fresh proposed rule it stated could save $90 billion over ten years through increased oversight and prevention of fraud and improper payments.

Industry observers note that the Comprehensive Regulations to Uncover Suspicious Healthcare (CRUSH) proposed rule, shared late Monday, spans Medicare, Medicaid, the Children’s Health Insurance Program (CHIP) and the Health Insurance Marketplace. It follows a request for information the administration circulated back in February. CMS it intends to conduct similar program integrity rulemaking “on an annual basis going forward.”.

Among the highlights: stiffer provider screening and safeguards for Medicare enrollment, a new regulatory framework for reporting and returning self-identified Medicaid fee-for-service overpayments similar to those in other programs, and requirements that Medicaid managed care plans report beneficiary deaths or address changes within 30 days to help CMS better spot improper payments.

“When President Trump called upon the federal government to crush fraud, waste, and abuse, CMS got right to work, using every tool at its disposal to achieve historic savings,” CMS Administrator Mehmet Oz, M.D., said in the agency’s announcement of the proposed rule. “CRUSH would build on those results by giving us stronger tools to prevent fraud, remove bad actors, and protect the Americans who rely on these programs. Whether criminals are billing Medicare for nonexistent canes and wheelchairs, fraudulently enrolling healthy seniors in Medicare-funded hospice care, or signing people up for Marketplace looks without their consent, the CRUSH proposed rule would give CMS stronger authority to stop these schemes and hold those responsible accountable.”.

The additional guardrails are expected to cost the government about $378.5 million over the same 10-year period CMS expects to save nearly $90 billion, according to the proposed rule.

It has been revealed that CMS, in its release and a lengthy fact sheet outlining the proposed changes, said it wants to revision Medicare provisions to tighten Medicare Advantage (MA) Adjustment Data Validation audits so that it can better spot cases in which diagnoses are not supported by medical documentation, thereby bumping up risk scores and payments. It also wants to increase suspicious activity reporting requirements for MA organizations and Part D blueprint sponsors, require some MA plan providers and suppliers to also enroll in Original Medicare for credential verification and guard seniors from unsolicited outreach from medical supply companies.

In Medicaid and CHIP, the agency wants to make it easier for states to join in on suspected schemes while fleshing out their data collection and reporting. CMS also wants to add provider enrollment termination grounds similar to those in Medicare.

Industry observers note that within the marketplace, CMS remarked it wants to begin restricting access for agents and brokers with certain felony convictions or other healthcare program exclusions on their record. The agency is also looking to bolster its authority to suspend and terminate, and to do so more swiftly.

“President Trump directed us to stop fraud, waste, and abuse, and the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services is taking action to protect taxpayer dollars,” HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. said in the announcement. “CRUSH would give CMS stronger tools to block fraudulent payments, remove dishonest providers, and protect Americans from schemes that exploit their healthcare coverage.

Public comment on the proposed rule, which includes more potential changes and a breakdown of the expected savings and costs, will be open through Jan. 19, 2027.

The program integrity proposed rule landed the same day CMS released its estimates on improper payments during fiscal year 2026.

Improper payments are those that do not meet the agency’s program requirements, and can include overpayments or underpayments alike. They are not necessarily a measure of fraud, though “some improper payments may involve fraud or abuse” alongside administrative errors, CMS remarked.

It has been revealed that in total, the agency outlined about $112.9 billion in estimated overpayments, an increase over the roughly $96.1 billion estimated for the prior fiscal year. That broke down into:.

CMS noted that the estimates are tied to claims submitted from July 1, 2024 through June 30, 2025, a period “before many of CMS’ current crushing fraud initiatives were implemented.” Those and other efforts will begin appearing in next year’s improper payment data, it said.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that if you missed the boat on this uniquely specced 1969 Shelby GT500, fret not, for Bring a Trailer has a 1968 GT500KR (King of the Road) up for grabs, with an odometer reading of 60,000 miles and a bid price currently sitting at $77,777. Featuring a 428-cubic-inch Cobra Jet V8 and finished in Wimbledon White with blue stripes, this GT500 is one of 1,053 KR fastbacks produced between April and July 1968. The Cobra Jet is paired with a four-speed manual, making this one of 530 four-speed KR fastbacks. Sure, Carroll Shelby made a lot of cool cars, but the fact that this GT500 also has the legend's signature on the dash panel takes the specialty factor even further.

According to recent reports, the reproduction data plate reveals the GT500KR was indeed a Wimbledon White example from the factory, and the blue stripes were added later by a previous owner. The description also mentions that the original owner used to race the car and that it has a replacement engine block, mentioned to have been installed during the late 1960s. This Shelby comes with power steering, power front disc brakes, and a 3.50:1 Traction-Lok differential from the factory. On the outside, the GT500KR's 15-inch alloy wheels, which the seller notes Shelby American refinished in 2005, sport Shelby center caps and feature BFGoodrich tires. Other exterior highlights include the grille-mounted Lucas fog lights, a rear spoiler, and a fiberglass hood with a working ram-air scoop.

The cabin is done in black knit-insert vinyl, covering both the front buckets and the Sport Deck rear seat. It also features the Interior Décor Group, which brings woodgrain accents to the dash, console, and doors, as well as the Visibility Group, which adds under-dash courtesy lamps along with lights for the glovebox, trunk, and engine bay.

It has been revealed that A 2017 inspection report of the car by Kevin Marti highlights past rust repair and some Bondo. Notably, the battery-tray fender apron isn't original. According to the description, the car's engine and transmission were resealed in 2016, and in June of 2017, California emissions equipment was added. The seller mentions that the fuel cap, antenna, and fuel door were replaced recently, as were the starter and starter solenoid. While the selling dealer is a BaT Local Partner from Florida, the car has an Arkansas title.

Recent findings suggest that there are 11 bids on this GT500 so far. But the current bid price seems quite low, at least for now, given that Hagerty's Price Guide puts a '68 GT500KR fastback in good condition between $117,000 and $140,000, and between $89,000 and $108,000 for a fair-condition car. The highest Hagerty reckons a concours-condition GT500KR fastback could be worth is around $235,000. What's interesting, however, is that this very GT500KR was previously sold for $201,000 on BaT in April 2022. And the car was featured again on the website in August 2026 but didn't quite meet the reserve, despite bids reaching as high as $240,000.

Whether this example will sell for its current bid price remains to be seen. Judging from its recent August appearance, though, that seems unlikely. If you fancy the car, go ahead and place your bid. The auction ends on Friday, November 27.

AGCO Celebrates Construction Milestone at Olmedo Solar Project in Spain

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, OLMEDO, Spain, Nov. 19, 2026 — AGCO (NYSE: AGCO) today unveiled that Project Olmedo, the solar installation at the center of its first Virtual Power Purchase Agreement (VPPA), has completed construction and commissioning and is expected to begin delivering renewable electricity to the Spanish power grid in the coming months, pending final regulatory approvals. BRUC, one of the largest renewable energy groups in Spain, built the latest solar installation in the northwest province of Valladolid.

It has been revealed that the milestone follows AGCO’s September 2025 announcement of its 10-year VPPA with BRUC. The installation’s two solar projects, Los Silos and El Granero, span approximately 300 hectares (741 acres) and hold approximately 150,000 solar panels. AGCO’s portion of the installation’s annual production is expected to be approximately 150 gigawatt-hours (GWh) of renewable electricity a year, equivalent to the annual electricity consumption of approximately 40,000 European households, based on Eurostat data.

“Project Olmedo will give AGCO long-term price certainty for the majority of the electricity certificate cost in Europe,” mentioned Tim Millwood, Senior Vice President, Chief Supply Chain Officer. “In volatile energy markets, securing that stability for 10 years strengthens the resilience of our supply chain while supporting new renewable generation.”.

A VPPA lets a company support upcoming renewable energy projects without taking direct delivery of the electricity they generate. Because AGCO’s agreement supported the construction of a brand-new installation, it will add new renewable capacity to the grid rather than drawing on existing sources, a principle known as additionality. The agreement also helps reduce AGCO’s Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions from purchased electricity in its Europe/Middle East (EME) region and supports its commitment to reduce absolute Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 55% by 2033 from a 2022 baseline.

According to recent reports, “Additionality is what makes this agreement truly meaningful,” remarked Roger Batkin, Senior Vice President, Corporate Affairs, General Counsel & Corporate Secretary. “We did not simply buy renewable electricity that already existed; we supported the construction of a brand-new renewable solar project. Accomplishing this project required over two years of involvement from many teams, functions, and areas of expertise across AGCO, along with technical advisory support from Schneider Electric and a strong partnership with BRUC.”.

Reflecting AGCO’s Farmer-First strategy, Project Olmedo supports local farmers to further diversify their land use by leasing land for the project while maintaining the option for livestock to graze among the panels, maintaining the vegetation in place of machinery.

AGCO and BRUC leaders, joined by local community representatives José Emilio Escudero García, Mayor of Bocigas, and Ursino Vara Pérez, Mayor of Almenara de Adaja, marked the milestone with a ribbon-cutting ceremony at the site in November. Additional drone footage from Project Olmedo and the ribbon-cutting event are available on AGCO’s YouTube page.

For more details on AGCO’s sustainability initiatives, visit the organization’s sustainability webpage and read the 2025 Sustainability Report. For more information about BRUC, visit the company’s website at brucenergy.com.

Recent findings suggest that AGCO (NYSE: AGCO) is a global leader in agricultural machinery and precision agriculture technologies. Driven by a Farmer-First strategy, AGCO delivers value through its differentiated leading brands, Fendt™, Massey Ferguson™, PTx™ and Valtra™. AGCO’s high-performance equipment and smart farming solutions, including brand-agnostic retrofit technologies and autonomous offerings, empower farmers to drive productivity while sustainably feeding the world. For more information, visit www.agcocorp.com.
